text:
incident-bot: ALERT: model-init high error rate in us-west-2. Symptoms: repeated deserialization failures, compile timeouts, and OOMs during warmup (affected pool: gen-large-01). Auto-escalation to P1 triggered.

oncall: seeing 503s to hosted endpoints that hit gen-large-01. customer impact: % of requests failing roughly 8% overall, spikes to 35% for a subset of low-latency customers.

eng-runtime-jess: confirming logs show two failure modes: (1) deserializing artifact blob fails with EOF / checksum mismatch, (2) subsequent compile step hangs then hits 60s timeout -> worker OOM while retrying. Looks like artifact corruption + memory spike during JIT kernels.

sre-mike: paging on-call for infra: today's node memory usage during warmup pushed paging to host NVMe -> spike in latencies. We need to stop warmups to that pool and drain traffic.

carla: @eng-runtime-jess can we hot-fallback to the smaller quantized variant (gen-medium-q4) for affected routes? That should reduce memory pressure and stop stampede.

eng-runtime-jess: yes. Preparing canary rollback -> switch model alias gen-large -> gen-medium-q4. Will keep KV cache warm for gen-medium. Rolling change via rollout service in 2m.

oncall: initiating traffic diversion. Putting gen-large-01 into maintenance and shifting new loads to gen-large-02 and eu-west for high-volume customers.

cs-liz: heads up to support: customers A and B seeing errors, opening incident comms. ETA for initial notice: 10m.

dan: pushing a mitigation script to evict corrupted artifacts from the artifact cache on the affected fleet nodes. Command:
```
# evict artifacts matching prefix
runtctl artifact evict --pool gen-large-01 --prefix models/gen-large/
```

eng-runtime-jess: also canceling ongoing JIT compiles on warmup threads to avoid further OOM. Patch applied to warmup controller: shorten compile timeout from 60s -> 10s and fall back to non-JIT path if compile fails.

sre-mike: performing live node-restarts on 3 hosts that reported paging spikes > 95% and high disk IO. Draining completed, restart in progress.

incident-bot: NOTE: Post-mitigation health checks show error rate down to 1.2% overall, customer-specific spikes reduced to <5%. Remaining errors are transient deserializations for older artifacts.

carla: can we add a temporary safety throttle on parallel warmups per node? Recommend max_concurrent_warmups=2 instead of 6.

eng-runtime-jess: agreed. Applying throttle across pool; patch rolling out. Also enabling fallback routing: if deserialization fails, immediate fallback to gen-medium-q4 instead of retrying heavy compile path.

cs-liz: draft sent for customer bulletin. Key points: brief outage window, mitigation steps taken, follow-up ticket to remediate artifact store checksum pipeline.

oncall: will keep the pool in maintenance for 30m and monitor. If stable, we'll do a controlled reload of artifacts after integrity checks.

dan: note from logs: sample stack for the OOMs:
```
runtime: allocate_kv_cache(268435456)
error: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
stack: warmup_worker -> jit_compile -> allocate_kv_cache
```
Also saw repeated "EOF while reading blob" before the compile attempts.

eng-runtime-jess: root cause hypothesis: partial artifact writes to s3 mirror triggered corrupted blobs; warmup kicks off compile which allocates large KV cache leading to immediate OOM on GPU, then paging. Remediation: (1) invalidate corrupted artifacts, (2) add write-verify on publish, (3) reduce warmup concurrency.

sre-mike: infra action items: isolate faulty hosts, run fs integrity on artifact mirror, and throttle warmup IO.

incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: evict-artifact, throttle-warmup, fallback-model-variant, restart-hosts, customer-notice.

carla: assigning follow-ups: ENG-RUNTIME-512 (add publish checksum verification), SRE-227 (artifact mirror fs check), OPS-88 (update warmup defaults).

oncall: moving to monitoring phase. If anyone sees error rate creep above 3% re-escalate. Great work team. :thumbsup:

cs-liz: I'll update customers in the morning with RCA and timeline for fixes.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status => mitigated. Will convert to postmortem if errors resurface.
